text:
cami: Heads up — seeing persistent jitter on shared-gpu-pool-3. p99 token latency jumped from ~65ms to ~220ms for a subset of sessions starting ~09:05 UTC. Not showing as CPU/VRAM spike in infra metrics. Anyone else seeing this?

raj: Seeing it too. Pulled a perf trace from host gpu-3a. KV cache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 61% around the same window.

lex: Can you paste the trace snippet and which kernel was selected? Could be a kernel flip or fallback.

cami: Trace snippet: ```
timestamp=2026-03-18T09:06:12Z host=gpu-3a pool=shared-gpu-pool-3
model=gpt-small kernel=amp_attn_v2 batch=1 seq=512
kv_hits=61 kv_slots=120k batch_latency_ms=180 prev_p99=65
```

sasha: I checked kernel_autoswitch logs — at 09:04:58 we had a fallback: amp_attn_v2 -> matmul_fallback triggered when seq-tail exceeded heuristic. That fallback path is ~3x slower for these small batches.

raj: Also see a small async memcpy backlog: async_prefetch_lag ~20ms on the same host around that time. Could be compounding.

zane: I reproduced locally with a synthetic mix of long and short sequences that alternated. Batching heuristics collapse and we start evicting KV because prefix reuse drops. When KV gets pressure, hit rate nosedives and kernel choice flips to safer slower path.

cami: That sounds like noisy-tenant behavior. Do we have a culprit tenant?

lex: Correlating tenant ids — tenant=acme-playground shows bursty patterns with many 1k-2k sequence requests starting 09:03 UTC. They had sustained bursts and no per-tenant slot cap on pool-3.

sasha: @infra-bot can you apply a soft throttle to acme-playground on pool-3 so we can verify mitigation? :thinking:

infra-bot: infra-bot: applied soft-rate-limit to tenant `acme-playground` (0.5 RPS) on pool-3 at 09:12 UTC. Monitoring metrics for 15m.

cami: :eyes: After the soft limit p99 on sampled hosts dropped to ~70ms and KV hit rate climbed back to ~89% for the affected window. Looks promising.

raj: So provisional root cause: combination of kernel-autoswitch sensitivity + KV cache eviction driven by low prefix reuse from a noisy tenant. Autoswitch picks fallback kernel under tail sequences and that increases latency further.

lex: Action items proposal: 1) Implement per-tenant KV partitioning or pinning of hot prefixes for high-volume tenants; 2) Soften the autoswitch threshold/introduce hysteresis for short bursts; 3) Add real-time sequence-length analyzer per tenant to auto-isolate when reuse falls below threshold. I'll start a PR for (2) and tests for alternating seq patterns.

sasha: I'll draft an operator runbook for immediate mitigations (soft-rate-limit, pool-migration, temporary KV-pin) and schedule follow-up to evaluate per-tenant cache slicing prototype.

zane: For long-term, we should also surface a small telemetry signal that flags rapid drops in KV hit-rate per-tenant so ops can triage before kernel flips.

cami: Thanks all — passing this to postmortem. Please add logs/traces to the incident doc. Closing the thread unless new findings.
